articles.title: One simple addition to postpartum care made a major difference

paras.en: One simple addition to postpartum care made a major difference
paras.zh: 产后护理的一个简单补充就产生了重大影响

paras.en: Patient navigators helped new mothers overcome healthcare barriers and stay connected to critical postpartum and primary care long after giving birth.
paras.zh: 患者导航器帮助新妈妈们克服医疗保健障碍，并在产后很长一段时间内与重要的产后和初级保健保持联系。

paras.en: - New mothers paired with patient navigators were much more likely to receive postpartum care, depression screening, preventive testing, and ongoing primary care. By helping with barriers such as transportation, childcare, scheduling, and confusing medical information, navigators may provide a powerful way to improve womenâs long-term health.
paras.zh: - 与患者导航员配对的新妈妈更有可能接受产后护理、抑郁症筛查、预防性测试和持续的初级护理。通过帮助克服交通、儿童保育、日程安排和混乱的医疗信息等障碍，导航器可能会提供一种改善女性长期健康的有力方法。

paras.en: Becoming a mother can be difficult under any circumstances, but for some women, everyday obstacles can make getting medical care after childbirth especially challenging. Limited health literacy, unreliable transportation, difficulty navigating a complicated healthcare system, lack of childcare, and unstable housing can all determine whether a new mother receives needed care or goes without it.
paras.zh: 在任何情况下，成为母亲都可能很困难，但对于一些女性来说，日常障碍可能会让产后获得医疗护理变得尤其困难。健康素养有限、交通不可靠、复杂的医疗保健系统难以驾驭、缺乏托儿服务以及不稳定的住房都可能决定新妈妈是否得到所需的护理。

paras.en: New research from Northwestern Medicine suggests that patient navigators can help remove many of those barriers. These trained guides work with patients and healthcare teams to connect people with medical care, services, and other resources. Among low-income pregnant individuals, the approach was linked to better postpartum health care and stronger connections to primary care that continued well beyond childbirth.
paras.zh: 西北医学的新研究表明，患者导航器可以帮助消除其中许多障碍。这些训练有素的指南与患者和医疗团队合作，将人们与医疗护理、服务和其他资源联系起来。在低收入孕妇中，这种方法与更好的产后医疗保健和与初级保健的更牢固的联系有关，这种联系在分娩后仍持续很长时间。

paras.en: The study was published Oct. 2 in JAMA Health Forum. According to the researchers, it is among the first studies to describe what an ideal model of postpartum care in the U.S. could look like.
paras.zh: 该研究于 10 月 2 日发表在《JAMA 健康论坛》上。研究人员表示，这是最早描述美国理想产后护理模式的研究之一。

paras.en: Patient Navigators Improved Postpartum Care
paras.zh: 患者导航器改善产后护理

paras.en: Compared with patients who received usual postpartum care without a patient navigator, those who worked with a navigator were more likely to:
paras.zh: 与在没有患者导航仪的情况下接受常规产后护理的患者相比，使用导航仪的患者更有可能：

paras.en: - Attend postpartum care visits (96% vs. 80% among those receiving usual postpartum care without a patient navigator)
paras.zh: - 参加产后护理就诊（在没有患者导航仪的情况下接受常规产后护理的患者中，这一比例为 96% 对比 80%）

paras.en: - Be counseled about all needed postpartum topics (65% vs. 51%)
paras.zh: - 获得有关所有需要的产后主题的咨询（65% 与 51%）

paras.en: - Have screening and care for postpartum depression (86% vs. 72%) in the critical "fourth trimester" months
paras.zh: - 在关键的“妊娠第四期”月份对产后抑郁症进行筛查和护理（86% 对比 72%）

paras.en: - Attend a primary care visit (57% vs. 30%) at one year after giving birth
paras.zh: - 产后一年参加初级保健就诊（57% vs. 30%）

paras.en: - Be using their desired family planning method, such as birth control, at one year to help space out their pregnancies (65% vs. 43%)
paras.zh: - 在一年内使用他们想要的计划生育方法，例如节育，以帮助间隔怀孕时间（65% vs. 43%）

paras.en: - Receive preventive health testing (i.e. blood pressure (85% vs 62%), lipids (28% vs 13%) and glucose (31% vs 16%)
paras.zh: - 接受预防性健康测试（即血压（85% vs 62%）、血脂（28% vs 13%）和血糖（31% vs 16%）

paras.en: "Pregnancy and the postpartum periods are complex, and people often deprioritize themselves, particularly if they don't have much support or have complex social needs," said corresponding author Dr. Lynn Yee, chief of maternal-fetal medicine in the department of obstetrics and gynecology at Northwestern University Feinberg School of Medicine and a Northwestern Medicine physician. "Combined with a fragmented healthcare system, many people do not receive the care they need."
paras.zh: “怀孕和产后时期很复杂，人们常常会降低自己的优先级，特别是当他们没有太多支持或有复杂的社会需求时，”通讯作者、西北大学范伯格医学院妇产科母胎医学主任、西北医学医师 Lynn Yee 博士说。 “再加上分散的医疗保健系统，许多人没有得到他们需要的护理。”

paras.en: "That makes a perfect storm of suboptimal women's health in this very key postpartum period, which is when we know many women drop out of care. If we can address this gap early and sustain their engagement with healthcare, we can make a difference in the health and well-being of women over the long run."
paras.zh: “在这个非常关键的产后时期，这使得女性的健康状况不佳，这是一场完美的风暴，我们知道很多女性在这个时期放弃了护理。如果我们能够及早解决这一差距并维持她们对医疗保健的参与，从长远来看，我们可以为女性的健康和福祉带来改变。”

paras.en: Patient navigation is already widely used in cancer care and is even funded by Medicaid, Yee said. However, the approach has received far less attention in postpartum care and has remained both understudied and underused.
paras.zh: Yee 说，患者导航已经广泛应用于癌症护理，甚至得到了医疗补助的资助。然而，该方法在产后护理中受到的关注要少得多，并且仍然没有得到充分研究和利用。

paras.en: The researchers said this is the first large-scale study to investigate the benefits of patient navigation among pregnant and postpartum individuals. The results could provide a foundation for additional research and potentially support future funding for postpartum navigation programs.
paras.zh: 研究人员表示，这是第一项调查孕妇和产后个体导航的好处的大规模研究。研究结果可以为进一步的研究奠定基础，并有可能为未来的产后导航项目提供资金支持。

paras.en: How Patient Navigators Helped New Mothers
paras.zh: 耐心导航员如何帮助新妈妈

paras.en: The study included 405 pregnant individuals receiving care at Prentice Women's Hospital in Chicago between 2020 and 2024. Participants assigned a patient navigator began working with that person near the end of pregnancy and continued receiving support throughout the first year after delivery.
paras.zh: 该研究纳入了 2020 年至 2024 年间在芝加哥 Prentice 妇女医院接受护理的 405 名孕妇。参与者指定一名患者导航员，在怀孕快结束时开始与该人一起工作，并在分娩后的第一年继续接受支持。

paras.en: The navigators spoke both English and Spanish and worked closely with patients to develop postpartum care plans, which were also shared with the medical team. They scheduled and attended appointments, helped coordinate transportation and childcare, communicated with doctors and nurses, and helped patients make sense of complicated medical information. They also worked to strengthen health literacy and give patients greater confidence in managing their own care.
paras.zh: 导航员会讲英语和西班牙语，并与患者密切合作制定产后护理计划，并与医疗团队分享。他们安排和参加预约，帮助协调交通和儿童保育，与医生和护士沟通，并帮助患者理解复杂的医疗信息。他们还努力加强健康素养，让患者更有信心管理自己的护理。

paras.en: The transition from pregnancy care to primary care can have important long-term consequences. Previous research has shown that complications such as gestational diabetes and preeclampsia can affect health years later, making continued medical follow-up especially important.
paras.zh: 从妊娠护理到初级护理的转变可能会产生重要的长期后果。先前的研究表明，妊娠糖尿病和先兆子痫等并发症可能会在数年后影响健康，因此持续的医疗随访尤为重要。

paras.en: Even people who have healthy pregnancies can encounter serious challenges after delivery. Postpartum depression, limited partner support, housing problems, domestic violence, and other unmet social or safety needs can make it harder for new mothers to prioritize their own health, Yee said.
paras.zh: 即使怀孕健康的人在分娩后也会遇到严峻的挑战。伊说，产后抑郁症、有限的伴侣支持、住房问题、家庭暴力以及其他未满足的社会或安全需求可能会让新妈妈更难优先考虑自己的健康。

paras.en: The researchers said the program's success in connecting postpartum patients with primary care demonstrates how navigators may help close some of these gaps.
paras.zh: 研究人员表示，该计划成功地将产后患者与初级保健联系起来，这表明导航器可以如何帮助缩小其中一些差距。

paras.en: "Cumulatively not engaging in health-promotion behaviors in the postpartum period has reverberating implications for the family unit, too," Yee said.
paras.zh: “在产后期间不参与促进健康的行为对家庭单位也会产生影响，”Yee 说。

paras.en: The benefits were not limited to patients. The study found that healthcare professionals also valued the support provided by navigators.
paras.zh: 好处不仅限于患者。研究发现，医疗保健专业人员也重视导航员提供的支持。

paras.en: For example, if a patient was unable to attend an appointment, a navigator could notify the doctor, arrange a new appointment, or handle administrative tasks that might otherwise fall to clinical staff. Navigators also helped make sure patients completed important follow-up steps after appointments, including glucose tolerance testing and subsequent medical visits.
paras.zh: 例如，如果患者无法参加预约，导航员可以通知医生、安排新的预约或处理原本可能由临床工作人员承担的管理任务。导航器还帮助确保患者在预约后完成重要的后续步骤，包括葡萄糖耐量测试和随后的就诊。

paras.en: "One of the goals of navigators was not just to help patients, but to help clinicians too, and doctors were happy at how much more efficient and engaged patients were," said co-author Joseph Feinglass, research professor of general internal medicine at Feinberg.
paras.zh: “导航员的目标之一不仅是帮助患者，还帮助临床医生，医生们对患者的效率和参与度大大提高感到高兴，”合著者、范伯格普通内科研究教授约瑟夫·芬格拉斯 (Joseph Feinglass) 说。

paras.en: Before taking part in the study, patient navigator Viridiana Carmona-Barrera had worked in hospital, insurance and women's health settings. That background gave her experience with many of the obstacles pregnant patients can encounter.
paras.zh: 在参与这项研究之前，患者导航员 Viridiana Carmona-Barrera 曾在医院、保险公司和妇女健康机构工作。这种背景让她经历了怀孕患者可能遇到的许多障碍。

paras.en: She recalled helping one pregnant patient with chronic health conditions who was in danger of missing an important appointment because she lacked reliable transportation and childcare. After other attempts to reach a solution were unsuccessful, Carmona-Barrera coordinated both transportation and childcare so the patient could make the appointment.
paras.zh: 她回忆起帮助一名患有慢性疾病的孕妇的经历，她因缺乏可靠的交通和儿童保育而面临错过重要预约的危险。在其他尝试达成解决方案失败后，卡莫纳-巴雷拉协调了交通和儿童保育，以便患者可以预约。

paras.en: "I like being someone who can help make these processes easier," Carmona-Barrera said. "As committed as health care organizations are to supporting patients, navigating the system can still be challenging."
paras.zh: “我喜欢成为能够帮助简化这些过程的人，”卡莫纳-巴雷拉说。 “尽管医疗保健组织致力于支持患者，但驾驭该系统仍然具有挑战性。”

paras.en: An important goal of the program was not to make patients permanently dependent on navigators. Instead, the researchers wanted participants to become more comfortable interacting with the healthcare system and more capable of managing their own care.
paras.zh: 该计划的一个重要目标是不让患者永远依赖导航仪。相反，研究人员希望参与者能够更轻松地与医疗保健系统互动，并且更有能力管理自己的护理。

paras.en: By building those skills over the first year after childbirth, the team hoped patients would eventually feel confident arranging appointments, seeking primary care, and navigating the healthcare system without additional assistance.
paras.zh: 通过在产后第一年培养这些技能，该团队希望患者最终能够自信地安排预约、寻求初级保健以及在没有额外帮助的情况下使用医疗保健系统。

paras.en: "Their goal was to put themselves out of business, to be able to get to the end of the year and say, 'You don't need me anymore,'" Yee said. "That's success for a navigation program."
paras.zh: “他们的目标是让自己破产，以便能够到年底说，‘你不再需要我了，’”易说。 “这就是导航计划的成功。”

paras.en: Materials provided by Northwestern University. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
paras.zh: 材料由西北大学提供。注意：内容可能会根据样式和长度进行编辑。

Grobman. Patient Navigation and Postpartum Health Care Outcomes. JAMA Health Forum, 2026; 7 (10): e263338 DOI: 10.1001/jamahealthforum.2026.3338
